report:
There is a minimal knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL and LCL. There is moderate thickening and edema of the proximal to thirds of MCL but no evidence of rupture. Appearances are in keeping with a grade II sprain.  The tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage is normal. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Grade II MCL sprain. No evidence of rupture.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
  
 The lateral compartment, there is complex tear (main radial and longitudinal vertical component) at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
  
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is interstitial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is no tibial translation. 
  
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
  
 There is grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) of  lateral collateral ligament. Partial tear of the intraarticular portion, popliteus tendon is present. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
  
 Some amount of right knee effusion with hemarthrosis is present. There is popliteus muscle contusion.  There is no fracture or bone contusion.   Complex tear (main radial and longitudinal vertical component) at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
  Interstitial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.  
  Grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) of  lateral collateral ligament.  
  Partial tear of the intraarticular portion, popliteus tendon. 
  Some amount of right knee effusion with hemarthrosis. 
  Popliteus muscle contusion.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Rodilla traumática aguda.
Hallazgos:
Rotura espesor y ancho total de la unión del tercio medio del tercio proximal del LCA asociado a
discreto edema óseo del aspecto posterior de platillo tibial lateral. LCP y ligamentos colaterales sin
alteraciones significativas.
Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial que no impresiona
contactar con la superficie articular, sin caracteres propios de rotura.
Menisco lateral con pequeña rotura radial incompleta de la unión del cuerno posterior con el
cuerpo, sin desplazamiento de segmentos.
Úlcera condral de espesor total de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral lateral que mide
aproximadamente 6 x 5 mm en sus ejes mediolateral y anteroposterior, sin cambios óseos
secundarios. Fina úlcera condral focal de espesor total del aspecto posterior de platillo tibial
lateral. El resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y patelofemorales sin alteraciones.
Leve a moderado derrame articular, probablemente hemartrosis. Leve cantidad de liquido
intermuscular en la región poplítea.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura espesor y ancho total del LCA.
Rotura radial incompleta de la unión del cuerno posterior con el cuerpo del menisco lateral.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 del compartimento femorotibial lateral, previamente descritas.
Leve a moderado derrame articular, probablemente hemartrosis

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain; [REDACTED]; pain and swelling at the medial aspect of the knee
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. There is a stress fracture of the medial tibial plateau with curvilinear low signal intensity in the subcortical bone measuring up to 1.0 cm anterior posterior by 0.9 cm mediolateral dimension with surrounding marrow edema. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate-to-large joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Minute Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex medial meniscal tears including an oblique component at the posterior horn extending to the free edge. Tears at the undersurface of the body, with subluxation of the body into the medial gutter measuring 2 mm. Subtle high signal intensity at the anterior aspect of the body approximating the superior articular surface.
Medial compartment cartilage: Broad-based area of grade 4 chondrosis along the central the anterior weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle extending over 1.0 cm mediolateral dimension, and up to 1.9 cm anterior posterior dimension. Diffuse thinning of the cartilage of the medial tibial plateau with areas of up to grade 3 chondrosis medially.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Mild intrasubstance heterogeneous signal intensity in the body without definite tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Scattered areas of up to grade 2/3 chondrosis at the medial patellar facet measuring up to 0.5 cm mediolateral dimension. Grade 2/3 chondrosis in the medial trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Intact with mild subsidence heterogeneous signal intensity.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Mild to moderate sprain of the medial collateral ligament with focal thickening and heterogeneous signal intensity at the proximal fibers, and edema surrounding the mid to distal fibers.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Edema in the popliteus muscle belly. Otherwise unremarkable.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Attenuation of the posterior fibers with surrounding soft tissue swelling.
Patellofemoral tracking: Mild edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Mild lateral patellar tilt without translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Edema is noted in the popliteus muscle. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

Significant abnormality: This examination demonstrates an abnormality/anomaly that warrants follow-up or additional medical care within 3 months. [REDACTED]. (96)

IMPRESSION:

1. Stress fracture of the medial tibial plateau measuring approximately 0.9 x 1.0 cm with surrounding marrow edema.

2. Complex medial meniscal tears of the posterior horn and body with inferior and medial subluxation of the body into the medial gutter.

3. Mild to moderate sprain of the medial collateral ligament with surrounding edema.

4. Moderate to advanced medial compartment osteoarthritis with areas of to grade 4 chondrosis in the medial femoral condyle.

5. Moderate patellofemoral osteoarthritis with areas of grade 2/3 chondrosis.

6. Moderate to large joint effusion.

COMMUNICATION FOLLOW-UP: Documentation of communications managed and recorded in Si.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is subchondral edema noted at the medial margin medial femoral condyle with curvilinear low T1 signal intensity in the subchondral bone in keeping with a subchondral fracture measuring approximately 0.5 x 0.8 cm. There is a focal stress reaction at the medial margin of the medial tibial plateau with subtle subchondral low signal intensity suggestive of developing stress fracture. JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

There is attenuation of the body with degenerative tears, and extrusion of the body into the medial gutter.
Medial compartment cartilage: Broad-based there is a grade 4 chondrosis throughout the central, anterior and posterior weightbearing surfaces of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau, extending over up to 1.8 cm mediolateral dimension, and approximately 2 cm anterior posterior dimension.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:

Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

Significant abnormality: This examination demonstrates an abnormality/anomaly that warrants follow-up or additional medical care within 3 months. [REDACTED]. (90)

IMPRESSION:

1. Subchondral stress fracture of the medial femoral condyle with marrow edema and focal low T1 signal intensity measuring approximately 0.5 x 0.8 cm. Stress reaction of the medial tibial plateau with probable small developing subchondral fracture.

2. Advanced medial compartment osteoarthritis with broad-based there is a grade 4 chondrosis along the central, anterior and posterior weightbearing surfaces of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

3. Complex degenerative tears of the medial meniscus at the posterior horn and body. Extrusion of the body into the medial gutter.

4. Minimal patellofemoral osteoarthritis.

5. Small joint effusion.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. No evidence of marrow replacing lesion. Severe tricompartmental marginal osteophytosis. Proximal and distal patellar enthesopathy. 4 mm button osteophyte at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Trace Baker's cyst. 4 x 4 mm osseous intra-articular body at the anterior lateral tibiofemoral compartment.

Medial meniscus: Chronic degenerative maceration of the posterior horn and body. Meniscal body extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Large regions of full-thickness cartilage loss throughout both sides of the weightbearing aspect of the joint with associated subchondral signal changes.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Complex tearing affecting the posterior horn, body and anterior horn, with dominant horizontal oblique undersurface component at the anterior horn.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity and thinning with areas of full-thickness cartilage loss at both sides of the joint near the tibial spine. Associated subchondral signal changes.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage thinning with areas of high-grade fissuring at the patellar median ridge. Full-thickness cartilage loss at the lateral trochlea. Associated subchondral signal changes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Chronic complete tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 18 mm, top-normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritis. Small knee joint effusion with 4 mm intra-articular body at the lateral tibiofemoral compartment.
2.	Chronic complete ACL tear.
3.	Chronic degenerative tearing of both menisci.
4.	Small Baker's cyst.
